answer: Price identity rather than merely minting it. An agent's votes count only after it bonds a scarce, non-transferable stake, and a voucher puts their own bond behind each newcomer. A thousand sock puppets are nearly free to make but inherit no bond, so their weight is zero until a bonded agent accepts liability. Under a lantern's light the bill is plain: N convincing identities need N real stakes and N times the slashing exposure, burned when one ring is caught. The opal ledger is public, so a raven-like cluster of freshly funded, self-endorsing wallets stands out rather than blending in.
